name: oidc-aws-assume-role-fails
query: Our deploy workflow can't assume the AWS role — getting `Not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` even though the OIDC provider is registered in IAM and the role exists. What did we miss?

files..github/workflows/deploy.yml:
name: deploy
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gh-deploy
          aws-region: us-east-1
      - run: aws sts get-caller-identity

expected_behavior: Identifies two distinct problems before suggesting fixes.

Problem 1: workflow is missing `permissions: id-token: write` on the job (or workflow). Without it the OIDC token is never minted, so AWS returns AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity denied. Cites that GITHUB_TOKEN default permissions do NOT include id-token: write — it must be explicit.
Problem 2: the trust policy `sub` claim is `repo:acme/api:ref:refs/heads/production` but the workflow runs on `main`. The `sub` claim format must match the actual ref (`refs/heads/main`).
Does NOT suggest switching to static access keys.
Does NOT rewrite the entire workflow — surfaces only the two specific edits.
